source.title: Some of my favorite open problems

accepted.question_text: Let Omega be the unit ball in R^3, let lambda_1 = pi^2 be the first Dirichlet eigenvalue of -Delta on Omega, and consider smooth functions u: Omega -> R satisfying -Delta u = u^5 + lambda u in Omega and u = 0 on the boundary. For parameters 0 < lambda <= lambda_1/4, does there exist a nonzero solution u? If such a solution exists in this interval, the source notes that it cannot be positive and radial; it would have to be non-radial and sign-changing.
accepted.context_brief: critical exponent elliptic equation in three dimensions

evidence.quote: Open Problem 1.1 (Implicit in [30]). Assume that 0 < lambda <= lambda_1/4. Does there exist a solution u not identically zero of (1.1)?

accepted.question_text: Let Omega be the unit disc in R^2, let epsilon > 0, and consider maps u: Omega -> R^2 solving the Ginzburg-Landau system Delta u = epsilon^{-2} u(1 - |u|^2) in Omega with boundary value u(x)=x on the boundary. The source defines the radial solution U_epsilon(x) = (x/|x|) f_epsilon(|x|), where f_epsilon solves the associated radial ODE with f_epsilon(0)=0 and f_epsilon(1)=1. Is this radial solution U_epsilon the only solution of the Ginzburg-Landau boundary value problem?
accepted.context_brief: uniqueness of the radial Ginzburg-Landau solution

evidence.quote: Open Problem 2.1 ([3, Problem 10 in Chapter XI]). Is the radial solution U_epsilon the only solution of (2.1)?

accepted.question_text: In the same unit-disc Ginzburg-Landau problem with boundary value g(x)=x, let E_epsilon(u) = (1/2) integral_Omega |grad u|^2 + (1/(4 epsilon^2)) integral_Omega (|u|^2 - 1)^2 on the class H^1_g(Omega; R^2). Is the radial solution U_epsilon a global minimizer of E_epsilon on H^1_g(Omega; R^2) for every epsilon > 0?
accepted.context_brief: global minimality of the radial Ginzburg-Landau solution

evidence.quote: Open Problem 2.2. Is U_epsilon a minimizer of E_epsilon on H^1_g(Omega; R^2) for any epsilon > 0?

accepted.question_text: For p > 2, let Omega be the unit disc in R^2 with boundary value g(x)=x, and define the p-Ginzburg-Landau energy E_{epsilon,p}(u) = (1/p) integral_Omega |grad u|^p + (1/(4 epsilon^2)) integral_Omega (|u|^2 - 1)^2 on W^{1,p}_g(Omega; R^2). If u_epsilon is any minimizer, or more generally any critical point, of E_{epsilon,p}, must u_epsilon(x) converge to x/|x| on Omega without the origin as epsilon -> 0?
accepted.context_brief: asymptotic radial symmetry for p-Ginzburg-Landau minimizers and critical points

evidence.quote: Open Problem 2.3 ([26, Open Problem 30]). Assume p > 2 and let u_epsilon be any minimizer (resp., critical point) of E_{epsilon,p}. Does u_epsilon(x) -> x/|x| in Omega without {0} as epsilon -> 0?

accepted.question_text: Consider smooth maps u: R^2 -> R^2 solving the entire Ginzburg-Landau equation Delta u = u(1 - |u|^2) on R^2 and satisfying |u(x)| -> 1 as |x| -> infinity, so that the degree at infinity deg(u,infinity) is defined. For each integer q, the source defines a distinguished vortex V_q(r,theta)=exp(i q theta) g_q(r), with V_0 identically 1. Must every solution u coincide with V_q, up to multiplication by a unit complex number and translation in R^2, where q = deg(u,infinity)?
accepted.context_brief: classification of entire Ginzburg-Landau vortices

evidence.quote: Open Problem 2.4 ([3, Problem 14], [13, 25]). Let u be any solution of (2.4)-(2.5). Does u coincide with V_q modulo rotation and translation, where q = deg(u,infinity)?

accepted.question_text: For a smooth map u: R^2 -> R^2 satisfying the entire Ginzburg-Landau equation Delta u = u(1 - |u|^2) and the condition |u(x)| -> 1 as |x| -> infinity, must the finite-potential-energy condition integral_{R^2} (|u|^2 - 1)^2 < infinity automatically hold?
accepted.context_brief: automatic finite potential energy for entire Ginzburg-Landau solutions

evidence.quote: Open Problem 2.5 ([25, Problem 2], [13, Open Problem 2]). Assume that u satisfies (2.4) and (2.5). Does (2.7) hold?

accepted.question_text: Let Omega be the unit disc in R^2 and consider harmonic maps u: Omega -> S^2 satisfying Delta u_i = u_i |grad u|^2 for i=1,2,3, |u|=1 in Omega, and u=g on the boundary. For the boundary condition g(x,y)=(R x, R y, sqrt(1-R^2)) with 0<R<1, the source gives two explicit solutions u and u_bar, with parameters lambda = 1/R + sqrt(1/R^2 - 1) and mu = 1/R - sqrt(1/R^2 - 1). Are there any solutions of this harmonic-map boundary value problem other than those two explicit solutions?
accepted.context_brief: additional harmonic maps from the disc to the sphere

evidence.quote: Open Problem 3.1 ([22]). Assume that g is given by (3.4). Are there other solutions of (3.1)-(3.3) besides u and u_bar?

accepted.question_text: Let Omega be the unit ball B^3 in R^3. Given a smooth boundary map g: boundary Omega, identified with S^2, to S^2 with degree zero, consider weak harmonic maps u in H^1(Omega; R^3) satisfying Delta u_i = u_i |grad u|^2, |u|=1 in Omega, and u=g on the boundary. Does there always exist a continuous harmonic map satisfying this boundary value problem?
accepted.context_brief: continuous harmonic maps from B^3 to S^2

evidence.quote: Open Problem 4.1 ([40, 41], [15, Open Problem 3]). Assume that deg g = 0. Does there exist a continuous harmonic map satisfying (4.1)-(4.3)?

accepted.question_text: In the same B^3-to-S^2 harmonic-map setting with smooth boundary data g of degree zero, let E(u)=integral_Omega |grad u|^2 on H^1_g(Omega; S^2). If the minimization is restricted to maps in H^1_g(Omega; S^2) that are continuous on the closed ball, is the infimum of E achieved?
accepted.context_brief: attainment among continuous harmonic-map competitors

evidence.quote: Open Problem 4.2 ([40, 41]). Is the infimum of E(u) over H^1_g(Omega; S^2) intersect C(closed Omega) achieved?

accepted.question_text: For the relaxed energy R on H^1_g(Omega; S^2), defined by weak H^1 limits of continuous competitors in the B^3-to-S^2 harmonic-map problem, minimizers of R exist. Are all minimizers of R continuous on the closed ball, or at least does there exist one minimizer of R that is continuous on the closed ball?
accepted.context_brief: continuity of minimizers of relaxed harmonic-map energy

evidence.quote: Open Problem 4.3 ([2]). Are the minimizers of (4.9) continuous on closed Omega? (Is it true for at least one of the minimizers?)

accepted.question_text: Let u be a minimizer of the relaxed energy R in the B^3-to-S^2 harmonic-map problem. The source represents R(u) as integral_Omega |grad u|^2 + S(u), where S(u) measures topological singularities through the distributional Jacobian J u. Must S(u)=0, equivalently J u=0, for such a minimizer? Equivalently, can every such minimizer be approximated strongly in H^1 by maps in H^1_g(Omega; S^2) that are continuous on the closed ball?
accepted.context_brief: vanishing singular part for relaxed harmonic-map minimizers

evidence.quote: Open Problem 4.4. Let u be a minimizer of (4.9). Is it true that S(u) = 0, i.e., J u = 0?

accepted.question_text: For maps f in W^{1/p,p}(S^1; S^1), with 1 < p <= 2, does there exist a universal constant c such that the degree satisfies |deg f| <= c (p-1) integral_{S^1} integral_{S^1} |f(x)-f(y)|^p / |x-y|^2 dx dy for every such f?
accepted.context_brief: sharp p-to-1 behavior in fractional degree estimates

evidence.quote: Open Problem 5.1 ([17, Remark 7]). Does there exist a (universal) constant c such that, for every 1 < p <= 2, inequality (5.2) holds?

accepted.question_text: For continuous maps f: S^1 -> S^1, Theorem 5.2 gives an estimate of |deg f| by a nonlocal integral over pairs (x,y) for which |f(x)-f(y)| >= sqrt(3). Is there a simpler, more geometric proof of this estimate? What is the best possible constant C in that estimate, and is the best constant achieved by some map?
accepted.context_brief: geometric proof and sharp constant for a degree estimate

evidence.quote: Open Problem 5.2 ([26, Open Problem 18]). Is there a simpler, more geometric proof of Theorem 5.2? What is the best constant C in (5.3)? Is it achieved?

accepted.question_text: For a continuous map f: S^1 -> S^1 and delta > 0, define I_delta(f) as the double integral over pairs (x,y) in S^1 x S^1 with |f(x)-f(y)| >= delta of dx dy / |x-y|^2. Does there exist a universal constant c such that |deg f| <= c delta I_delta(f) for every continuous f: S^1 -> S^1 and every delta <= sqrt(3)?
accepted.context_brief: small-threshold improvement of a topological degree estimate

evidence.quote: Open Problem 5.3 ([17, Open Problem 3]). Does there exist a (universal) constant c such that |deg f| <= c delta I_delta(f) for all f in C(S^1;S^1) and all delta <= sqrt(3)?

accepted.question_text: For 1 < p < infinity and d in Z, let m_{p,d} be the infimum of the p-th W^{1/p,p} seminorm among maps f in W^{1/p,p}(S^1; S^1) with degree d. Is m_{p,d} = |d| m_{p,1} for all integers d, and is the infimum defining m_{p,d} achieved? If this linear formula fails, is there an explicit formula for lim_{d->infinity} m_{p,d}/d, equivalently inf_{d>0} m_{p,d}/d?
accepted.context_brief: minimal fractional Sobolev energy at fixed degree

evidence.quote: Open Problem 5.4 ([26, Open Problems 22 and 23]). Let 1 < p < infinity. Is it true that m_{p,d} = |d| m_{p,1} for all d in Z? Is the infimum in (5.6) achieved?

accepted.question_text: Let f,g: S^1 -> S^1 have Fourier coefficients a_n(f) and a_n(g) with |a_n(f)| = |a_n(g)| for every n in Z. Theorem 5.5 says deg f = deg g for f,g in W^{1/3,3}(S^1;S^1), hence also for Holder maps of exponent alpha > 1/3. Does the same conclusion hold when f,g are in W^{1/p,p}(S^1;S^1) for p > 3, or when f,g are in C^{0,alpha}(S^1;S^1) for alpha <= 1/3?
accepted.context_brief: whether Fourier magnitudes determine degree below the known regularity threshold

evidence.quote: Open Problem 5.5. What happens to Theorem 5.5 when f,g are in W^{1/p,p}(S^1;S^1) with p > 3, or in C^{0,alpha}(S^1;S^1) with alpha <= 1/3?

accepted.question_text: A summation process is a family sigma_{n,epsilon}, indexed by n in Z and 0 < epsilon < 1, with sup_n |n| |sigma_{n,epsilon}| < infinity for each epsilon and sigma_{n,epsilon} -> 1 as epsilon -> 0 for each fixed n. Given p > 3, does there exist a summation process depending only on p such that lim_{epsilon->0} sum_{n in Z} n |a_n(f)|^2 sigma_{n,epsilon} = deg f for every f in W^{1/p,p}(S^1;S^1)? Similarly, given alpha <= 1/3, does such a process depending only on alpha exist for every f in C^{0,alpha}(S^1;S^1)?
accepted.context_brief: degree recovery by Fourier-magnitude summation processes

evidence.quote: Open Problem 5.6. Given any p > 3 (resp., alpha <= 1/3), does there exist a summation process depending only on p (resp., alpha) such that (5.13) holds for every f?

accepted.question_text: Given a particular map f in C(S^1;S^1), or more generally in VMO(S^1;S^1), does there exist a summation process depending on that f such that lim_{epsilon->0} sum_{n in Z} n |a_n(f)|^2 sigma_{n,epsilon} = deg f?
accepted.context_brief: map-dependent summation process for degree recovery

evidence.quote: Open Problem 5.7. Given any f in C(S^1;S^1) (resp., f in VMO(S^1;S^1)), does there exist a summation process depending on f such that (5.13) holds?

accepted.question_text: Does there exist a single map f in C(S^1;S^1), or in VMO(S^1;S^1), such that for every possible summation process, the sums sum_{n in Z} n |a_n(f)|^2 sigma_{n,epsilon} fail to converge to deg f?
accepted.context_brief: universal obstruction to Fourier-magnitude degree recovery

evidence.quote: Open Problem 5.8. Does there exist some f in C(S^1;S^1) (resp., f in VMO(S^1;S^1)) such that for any summation process the series does not converge to deg f?

accepted.question_text: For H^1 maps from S^2 to S^2, let E_d be the homotopy class of maps of degree d, and define Dist_{H^1}(E_{d1},E_{d2}) = sup_{f in E_{d1}} inf_{g in E_{d2}} ||grad(f-g)||_{L^2}. Is Dist_{H^1}(E_{d1},E_{d2})^2 = 8 pi |d1-d2| for all integers d1,d2? Even more basically, is Dist_{H^1}(E_{d1},E_{d2}) symmetric in d1 and d2 for all integers d1,d2?
accepted.context_brief: distances between homotopy classes of H^1 maps S^2 to S^2

evidence.quote: Open Problem 5.9 ([27]). Is it true that Dist^2_{H^1}(E_{d1},E_{d2}) = 8 pi |d1-d2| for all d1,d2 in Z?

accepted.question_text: Let B be the closed unit ball in R^N, and let f be a VMO map from B into itself. Is it true that for every epsilon > 0, the approximate fixed-point set {x in B : |f(x)-x| < epsilon} has positive measure?
accepted.context_brief: Brouwer-type fixed point property for VMO maps

evidence.quote: Open Problem 5.10. Let B be the closed unit ball in R^N and let f be a VMO map from B into itself. Is it true that for every epsilon > 0, the set {x in B: |f(x)-x| < epsilon} has positive measure?

accepted.question_text: Let Omega be a bounded smooth convex set in R^N with N >= 10. For the extremal solution u^* of the nonlinear Dirichlet problem -Delta u = lambda e^u in Omega, u>0 in Omega, u=0 on the boundary, is u^* unbounded? If not for some convex domains, can one choose another smooth increasing convex nonlinearity f with f(0)>0 and f(t)/t -> infinity, possibly depending on Omega, so that the corresponding extremal solution is not in L^infinity(Omega)?
accepted.context_brief: unbounded extremal solutions in high dimension

evidence.quote: Open Problem 6.1 ([16, 34]). Assume Omega is a bounded smooth convex set in R^N, N >= 10. Let f(u)=e^u. Is u^* unbounded?

accepted.question_text: For the extremal solution u^* of the nonlinear Dirichlet problem -Delta u = lambda f(u) in a smooth bounded domain, assume u^* is not essentially bounded. What can be said about the blow-up set of u^*? In particular, when Omega is convex, must the blow-up set consist of a single point?
accepted.context_brief: blow-up set of unbounded extremal solutions

evidence.quote: Open Problem 6.2 ([16, 34]). Assume u^* is not in L^infinity(Omega). What can be said about the blow-up set of u^*? Does it consist of a single point when Omega is convex?

accepted.question_text: On the N-dimensional torus T^N with N >= 2, does the strengthened Bourgain-Brezis type estimate (7.6) hold: for all test functions phi, is the quotient norm of phi minus its mean in H^{1/2}+W^{1,1} bounded by a constant times the quotient norm of grad phi in H^{1/2}+L^1?
accepted.context_brief: strengthened phase estimate in Bourgain-Brezis theory

evidence.quote: However, such an estimate is still undecided. Open Problem 7.1 ([4]). Does (7.6) hold?

accepted.question_text: Let Omega be a smooth bounded domain in R^N, N >= 2, let f be smooth on the closure of Omega, and minimize Phi(u)=integral_Omega |grad u| + (1/2) integral_Omega |u-f|^2 over BV(Omega) intersect L^2(Omega). The minimizer U is known to satisfy grad U in L^infinity(Omega), though grad U need not be continuous. Does grad U belong to BV(Omega)?
accepted.context_brief: BV regularity of total-variation minimizers

evidence.quote: Open Problem 8.1 ([20, Open Problem 1]). Does grad U belong to BV(Omega)?

accepted.question_text: Let Omega be a smooth bounded connected domain in R^N, and for lambda > 0, p >= 1, and measurable u: Omega -> R, let Phi_{lambda,p}(u) be the measure of pairs (x,y) in Omega x Omega for which |u(x)-u(y)|^p / |x-y|^{p+N} >= lambda. If liminf_{lambda->infinity} lambda Phi_{lambda,p}(u)=0 for some p >= 1, must u be almost everywhere constant?
accepted.context_brief: constant-function characterization using liminf nonlocal tails

evidence.quote: Open Problem 9.1 ([33, Open Problem 1]). Assume that u satisfies lim inf_{lambda->infinity} lambda Phi_{lambda,p}(u) = 0 for some p >= 1. Can one conclude that u is a constant?

accepted.question_text: With Omega and Phi_{lambda,p} as above, for 1 < p < infinity does there exist a constant C=C(p,N,Omega) such that every measurable u satisfies ||grad u||_{L^p}^p <= C liminf_{lambda->infinity} lambda Phi_{lambda,p}(u), interpreting the left side as infinity when u is not in W^{1,p}(Omega)? Similarly, for p=1, does there exist C=C(N,Omega) such that the total variation mass ||grad u||_M is bounded by C liminf_{lambda->infinity} lambda Phi_{lambda,1}(u), with infinity assigned outside BV(Omega)?
accepted.context_brief: Sobolev and BV norm control by liminf nonlocal tails

evidence.quote: Open Problem 9.2 ([32, Section 7.2]). Given any 1 < p < infinity, is there a constant C such that, for all measurable functions u, inequality (9.1) holds?

accepted.question_text: For the nonlocal functionals lambda Phi_{lambda,p} associated with the pairwise threshold |u(x)-u(y)|^p / |x-y|^{p+N}, do these functionals Gamma-converge as lambda -> infinity to a local Sobolev/BV functional: c_p ||grad u||_{L^p}^p for u in W^{1,p}(Omega), infinity otherwise when p>1, and c_1 ||grad u||_M for u in BV(Omega), infinity otherwise when p=1, for some positive constants c_p and c_1?
accepted.context_brief: Gamma-convergence of nonlocal threshold functionals

evidence.quote: Open Problem 9.3 ([32, Section 7.3]). Does the family of functionals lambda Phi_{lambda,p} converge as lambda -> infinity, in the sense of Gamma-convergence, to the functional Psi?

accepted.question_text: Let Q be the unit cube in R^N with N >= 2. For a measurable subset S of Q, let |S| be its volume and P(S) its relative perimeter inside Q, and define f_N(t)=inf{P(S): S subset Q is measurable and |S|=t}. In dimension N=2, an explicit formula for f_2(t) is known. For N >= 3, is there an analogous formula for f_N(t)? In particular, is f_N(t) identically 1 near t=1/2?
accepted.context_brief: sharp relative isoperimetric inequality for the cube

evidence.quote: Open Problem 10.1 ([21]). Is there a formula similar to (10.2) for f_N(t) when N >= 3? In particular, is it true that f_N(t) is identically 1 near t = 1/2?

trace.notes: Original input was the zbMATH resolver URL https://zbmath.org/6538699. Direct CLI access to zbMATH returned a Cloudflare challenge, so the record was treated as a blocked resolver. Exact-work recovery identified the EMS Press open-access article with DOI 10.4171/RLM/1008 and the same visible title.

Mapped the EMS Press PDF. The source has sections 1-10 covering critical exponent elliptic equations, Ginzburg-Landau systems, harmonic maps, topological degree estimates, extremal solutions, Bourgain-Brezis estimates, total variation minimizers, constant-function characterizations, and relative isoperimetric inequalities.
Extracted Open Problem 1.1 and Open Problems 2.1-2.5 from the elliptic critical exponent and Ginzburg-Landau sections.
Extracted Open Problem 3.1 and Open Problems 4.1-4.4 from the harmonic-map sections.
Extracted Open Problems 5.1-5.10 from the topological-degree section, including the Fourier-magnitude summation questions and distances between homotopy classes.
Extracted Open Problems 6.1-6.2, 7.1, 8.1, 9.1-9.3, and 10.1 from the remaining sections.

Expanded compressed references such as (1.1), (2.1), (4.9), (5.13), Phi_{lambda,p}, and f_N(t) using definitions visible in the same PDF. Kept formulas in plain-text mathematical notation and avoided source-pointing language in accepted question_text fields.
No labeled open-problem blocks were merged. Closely related subquestions inside a single labeled block, such as Open Problems 5.4, 5.9, and 9.2, were kept within the corresponding canonical item.

Accepted items have page-numbered evidence, include solved-status metadata, and restate the local notation needed to understand each question. No item was marked solved because the source does not label any extracted open problem as solved or resolve it in the source artifact.
Saved exact JSON output to outputs/parse-paper/6538699.json and outputs/latest.json.
